prize_parts.citation: for research showing how technological change and trade shocks reshape labour demand, wages and local labour markets

statement.case_for: B027 has the broadest influence of the shortlisted work and combines a clear conceptual framework with transparent empirical design. The task-based account of technology and the skills-demand lineage explain wage polarisation. The local labour-market evidence on import competition shows that adjustment to trade is persistent and geographically concentrated. The work reaches well beyond labour economics into trade, macro and political economy, and it has been replicated, extended and contested for roughly a decade or more, so its core findings are tested. Having listened to colleagues, I now think Autor, Hanson and Katz fit a single citation better than my opening trio of Autor, Dorn and Hanson. Katz anchors the skills, technology and wage-inequality strand that the shortlist label names. A trade-shock-only trio would credit one half of the achievement. Autor spans both strands and Hanson anchors the trade-shock evidence. Nine of eleven members proposed a set including Katz, but I treat that as a coincidence of views and not as evidence of merit. My reason is the match between the credited work and the citation.
statement.case_against: Attribution is the strongest reservation. The three-name limit omits David Dorn, a central co-author of the China-shock papers, and the task framework has other authors outside the credited names. Magnitudes and persistence of the China-shock effects remain debated, and some of the evidence is specific to one episode and period. The prize could also be judged to overlap with recent recognition of labour, education and technology work (Card 2021, Goldin 2023, Acemoglu 2024), and a citation that spans both strands may be read as two prizes combined.

responses.point: Krusell ranks B012 first and proposes only Autor and Hanson for B027. He sees the task and China-shock cores as separable, and he questions whether the shock papers are a prize-level conceptual advance or strong applied work.
responses.response: I agree that a two-person B027 would be the cleanest attribution for the trade-shock strand, and I take the applied-versus-conceptual worry seriously. I think the work is more than applied. The task framework and the local-labour-market design together supply an explanation with identification, and that combination is what changed practice. The same logic supports adding Katz, because leaving out the skills-demand lineage would credit only half of what the shortlist item describes. I also rank B012 second and regard Helpman and Melitz as a strong, mature claim. My preference for B027 rests on breadth of impact and on the extent to which its core findings have survived replication and critique, not on any view that heterogeneous-firm trade is weak.

responses.point: Hassler ranks B006 first. Kiyotaki and Moore's collateral-constraint mechanism is a foundational building block of macro-finance, and a two-person award would keep the attribution clean even though the 2022 prize overlaps in part.
responses.response: I accept that Kiyotaki-Moore is a clean attribution and a durable mechanism, and I ranked it sixth, not lower, for that reason. My reservation is about the weight of empirical confirmation. The mechanism is mainly theoretical and its quantitative importance is established indirectly, whereas B027 rests on directly examined and heavily scrutinised evidence. The 2022 overlap also lowers the marginal case for a macro-finance award this year. I do not think B006 is weak, and I would be comfortable with it as an alternative on a second look. I would still put the stronger evidence for lasting influence behind B027.

responses.point: Andersson ranks B018 first. The New Keynesian framework with Calvo pricing and policy rules is the core of how central banks think. He accepts that the choice of three from eight credited names is contestable.
responses.response: The influence of B018 is not in doubt, and I agree attribution is the main obstacle. My own research on price adjustment, including menu costs and asymmetric adjustment, makes me cautious about how much weight to place on time-dependent pricing as a validated mechanism. The empirical micro evidence on price setting does not support it uniformly, and that evidence is part of why I rank B018 fifth. A prize here would require the committee to settle a difficult three-name cut among Calvo, Taylor, Woodford, Galí, Christiano, Eichenbaum, Gertler and Smets. I see that as a bigger risk to a clear citation than the attribution problem in B027, which is limited to Dorn and the task-framework co-authors.

responses.point: Dreber-Almenberg ranks B027 first with Autor, Hanson and Katz, and she flags that Acemoglu's task-based work and the 2024 and 2025 prizes may complicate how the committee weighs the entry. She also notes that omitting Dorn is somewhat arbitrary.
responses.response: I agree with both points and treat them as unresolved. Acemoglu's task-based work is a parallel contribution, and the committee needs to decide whether his earlier recognition leaves the Autor-Katz task framework with a sufficiently distinct increment. I think it does, because the China-shock identification and the education-technology race are separate contributions, but that depends on how a citation is worded. I also agree that excluding Dorn is a real cost and that the boundary is imperfect. I would keep the citation worded around the findings on labour demand, wages and local labour markets, not around the task model, to limit the overlap problem.

uncertainties: Whether Dorn's contribution to the China-shock papers justifies Autor, Dorn and Hanson over Autor, Hanson and Katz if the committee prefers a trade-shock-only citation.
Whether Acemoglu's earlier recognition for task-based work leaves a distinct increment for the Autor-Katz task and skills framework.
The size and persistence of the China-shock effects and their external validity beyond the US episode.
Whether the committee would treat the technology and trade strands as one achievement or two.
How to weigh B006 against B027 given the 2022 prize overlap and the largely theoretical nature of Kiyotaki-Moore.
statement.conflict_note: I co-authored a 2026 IJIO paper with committee chair John Hassler and former chair Tore Ellingsen. My research on price adjustment, exchange-rate pass-through and invoicing currency is adjacent to B010, B012 and B018, though not to my preferred B027. I am married to Magdalena Andersson, a former Swedish prime minister. This is a public fact, and no bearing on any shortlisted candidate is apparent from the supplied profile. None of the credited names on the shortlist appears among my listed co-authors, so no specific candidate connection is apparent.
